2415.body:
"Double The Money" has two of three top prizes left and is about halfway through its run. About half of the tickets are already sold. As a game goes on, the same prizes are spread across fewer tickets. Right now, a larger share of the top prizes is left than of the tickets, which is a good sign.

If you play "Double The Money" often, bookmark this page. The write-up is updated with each morning's data.
2415.headline: Tickets sold so far

2416.body:
Of all the tickets printed for "Loaded with $2,000s", about a third are still unsold. The game is past the halfway point of its run, with 1,339 of 3,372 top prizes unclaimed. In every scratcher, either the tickets or the prizes run out first. The rest of this page shows the details.

Tomorrow's count on "Loaded with $2,000s" will be a little different. The game sells every day, and this page keeps track.
2416.headline: Where this game is in its run

2419.body:
"Bronze 7s" has fewer top prizes left. The count changed when one top prize of $2,777 was claimed last week. Unsold tickets still hold one of the original four. Check the top prize count first when you compare scratchers.

If you play "Bronze 7s" often, bookmark this page. The write-up is updated with each morning's data.
2419.headline: Fewer $2,777 prizes left

2420.body:
On "Silver 7s", one $177,777 top prize was claimed over a week ago. That leaves two of the original three. The prize table has today's count for every prize level.

Today's free summary of "Silver 7s" ends here. Every number behind it is on this page.
2420.headline: The top prize list got shorter

2421.body:
"Gold 7s" is down to one top prize after a $577,777 winner was claimed earlier this week. The game started with three top prizes. Know that before you buy, because a change in top prizes changes the whole game.

2421.headline: A player won a top prize

2422.body:
"Platinum 7s" has gone close to two months without a top prize claim, and tickets kept selling. Only a fixed number of tickets are printed. About half of the tickets are sold, and every remaining $2 million prize is still unclaimed. That leaves the same top prizes among fewer tickets.

Everything here about "Platinum 7s" comes from official Virginia lottery numbers, current through October 30.
2422.headline: Close to two months, no top prize claimed

2426.body:
"HAUNTED HUNDREDS" has 97,514 prizes of $2 still unclaimed, which is its most common win. Just below the top prize is the $50 prize, with 755 left. The full count for every prize level is listed below.

Today's free summary of "HAUNTED HUNDREDS" ends here. Every number behind it is on this page.
2426.headline: What's actually left to win

2427.body:
"HOLIDAY TRIPLER" is new from the Virginia Lottery. It is a $1 game with 602 top prizes of $300. Nothing big has been won yet because almost no one has played it. This page will show it when that changes.

Everything above about "HOLIDAY TRIPLER" comes from the Virginia Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
2427.headline: A brand-new game to watch

2428.body:
"PEPPERMINT PAYOUT" just reached Virginia stores with five top prizes of $25,000. A new game is the easiest kind to judge. No prizes have been claimed, and the printed odds are accurate for now. Every day of sales changes that, and this page tracks it.

Everything above about "PEPPERMINT PAYOUT" comes from the Virginia Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
2428.headline: A new game is here

2429.body:
"MERRY MONEY TREE" has joined the Virginia lineup at $5 with four top prizes of $125,000. Only on the first day do the printed odds describe the game exactly, because nothing has been won. Starting tomorrow, this page shows how that changes.

Every line of MERRY MONEY TREE's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
2429.headline: New in stores

"WRAPPED IN RICHES" just went on sale in Virginia. The game has ten full prize levels with three top prizes of $500,000. Every scratcher starts this way and loses prizes as it sells. You are seeing this one before that starts, when it is easiest to judge.
